race.name: Toppling Goliath Gravel Grinder
race.tagline: The Iowa Gravel Series championship: 100 kilometers of Driftless hills, brewery start and finish, and a hard 2:00 PM support horizon.

vitals.registration: $40 early or $50 late for the standard series entry; processing fees and optional meal or shirt packages are additional
vitals.prize_purse: Podium recognition for the first three men and women; no cash purse published
vitals.aid_stations: Two scheduled aid stations; the first closes at 10:00 AM and the second at noon
vitals.cutoff_time: Route sweep ends at 2:00 PM; riders still on course are on their own for support

climate.description: An October morning in the Driftless Area can begin cold and move through sun, wind, or rain before the afternoon support horizon.

terrain.surface: Driftless Area gravel roads with repeated hills
features: Group start on open rural roads
Toppling Goliath Brewing Company start and finish

gravel_god_rating.score_note: The series-championship role, detailed schedule, low entry price, Driftless setting, and brewery venue are meaningful strengths. A regional field, open roads, modest distance, and no published cash purse keep it in Tier 3.

biased_opinion.summary: Toppling Goliath Gravel Grinder is the October 10, 2026 Iowa Gravel Series championship in Decorah. The 100-kilometer race starts at 7:30 AM, climbs about 3,500 feet through the Driftless hills, and finishes at Toppling Goliath Brewing Company. The event is new to the series in 2026 but the organizer says this is the third year a race has started at the brewery.
strengths: Driftless hills in peak fall season
weaknesses: No published field list or cash purse
biased_opinion.bottom_line: This is a sharp regional championship rather than a destination epic. The value is excellent, the Driftless terrain is legitimate, and the published support clock makes steady pacing and efficient aid stops part of the race.

final_verdict.one_liner: A low-cost Iowa series championship with 3,500 feet of Driftless punch packed into 100 kilometers.
final_verdict.should_you_race: Race it if you want an organized, competitive fall gravel day with repeated hills, clear logistics, and a community finish. Choose the 50-kilometer route if the 2:00 PM support horizon makes the long course a poor fit.
final_verdict.alternatives: Waukon 100 for a longer Driftless test, Soldier Cutoff Hillduro for Loess Hills climbing, or Fairfield Harvest Rush for another late-season Iowa Gravel Series race.

history.founder: Iowa Gravel Series and local partners
history.origin_story: The organizer added the brewery-hosted race to the Iowa Gravel Series for 2026 after two prior editions from the same venue, making it the season championship while retaining Waukon 100 as a summer Driftless race.
notable_moments: 2026: First edition as the Iowa Gravel Series championship
history.reputation: A developing regional championship built around Decorah's Driftless gravel and a recognizable brewery venue.

course_description.character: The 100-kilometer race uses a group start from Toppling Goliath Brewing Company and accumulates about 3,500 feet across the Driftless hills. The organizer publishes aid windows and a 2:00 PM end to route sweep but not a mile-by-mile current course narrative.

suffering_zones.name: Opening Group Start
suffering_zones.description: A championship group start invites speed before the repeated climbing has accumulated.
suffering_zones.survival_strategy: Protect space, cap the early surges, and let the full 100 kilometers—not the first selection—set the pace.

suffering_zones.name: Driftless Repeats
suffering_zones.description: About 3,500 feet of gain arrives through repeated Iowa hills rather than one defining mountain.
suffering_zones.survival_strategy: Climb below threshold early, carry speed without reckless line choices, and fuel before the terrain makes eating inconvenient.

suffering_zones.name: Support Clock
suffering_zones.description: The second aid station closes at noon and route sweep ends at 2:00 PM.
suffering_zones.survival_strategy: Know the required average speed, keep stops deliberate, and carry enough food, fluid, navigation, and repair capacity to finish safely if support has moved on.

course_description.signature_challenge: Maintaining punchy-climb restraint and useful group speed while staying ahead of the noon aid closure and 2:00 PM support horizon.

guide_variables.race_terrain: Repeated Driftless Area hills on open rural gravel roads
race_challenges: Noon aid closure and 2:00 PM support horizon

source_review.facts_scope: The official event and series pages confirm the date, venue, 50- and 100-kilometer distances, exact starts, approximate climbing, packet schedule, aid windows, route-sweep horizon, championship role, entry structure, and third-year brewery-hosted lineage. The final route, surface percentages, field list, parking map, and participant instructions remain authoritative.

logistics.explanation: The organizer publishes Friday and race-morning packet pickup, exact starts, a 7:15 AM briefing, two aid windows, a 2:00 PM route-sweep horizon, one brewery venue, and lodging guidance. Final parking and participant instructions remain pending.

length.explanation: The flagship is approximately 62 miles, long enough for accumulated fatigue and meaningful fueling but well below ultra-distance gravel. A 50-kilometer option broadens access.

technicality.explanation: The organizer emphasizes gravel roads and Driftless hills, not singletrack or technical sectors. Open-road group dynamics and changing gravel demand attention without making this a technical-riding showcase.

elevation.explanation: About 3,500 feet in roughly 62 miles falls in the published 2,000-4,000-foot scoring band. The repeated Driftless hills still reward punchy durability without reaching mountain-event vertical.

climate.explanation: October in northeast Iowa can bring a cold start, wind, rain, or a warming afternoon. The risk is variable rather than extreme, so forecast-driven layers matter more than acclimation.

altitude.explanation: Decorah creates no altitude-acclimatization demand. Terrain density, open-road judgment, weather, and the support clock are the relevant constraints.

adventure.explanation: The Driftless Area gives the race a distinctive landscape of repeated hills and rural gravel. It is a strong regional setting without the remoteness or scale of a backcountry epic.

prestige.explanation: Championship status inside the Iowa Gravel Series adds stakes, and the venue has hosted two prior race editions. The event does not yet have a national field or long standalone history.

race_quality.explanation: The organizer publishes a detailed schedule, group starts, aid windows, route sweep, podium process, photos, and official results. The field list, final route, and cash awards are not published.

experience.explanation: A brewery start and finish, fall Driftless terrain, series finale, and two distance choices create a coherent regional race experience without destination-event production.

community.explanation: The Iowa Gravel Series centers accessible community racing, marked courses, aid, photography, timing, and post-race gathering. The brewery venue makes the finish part of the event rather than a parking-lot exit.

field_depth.explanation: Series-championship points should concentrate the regional field, but no 2026 start list, elite roster, or field cap is published.

value.explanation: The official series price begins at $40 for a marked, timed, aided race with photography, results, and podium recognition. That is exceptional current value.

expenses.explanation: Decorah is a driveable Midwest destination with camping and lodging options, a single start-finish venue, and no shuttle. October lodging and travel remain the main costs.
